subject: Polaris AI — Dedicated Capacity kickstart & GPU pool plan
messages:
From: Lisa Turner <lisa.turner@polaris-ai.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@polaris-ai.com
Date: 2027-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity kickstart — Polaris requirements and timeline

Hi Vanessa and Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. Per our internal planning, Polaris wants to move to a dedicated GPU pool for inference (initial target: recommender and chat feature set). High level needs: 
- Production target traffic: ~1.5M tokens/day peak; burst up to ~3M tokens/day during campaigns.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 120ms for short chat prompts (<= 256 tokens).
- Data: All inference logs must remain in our VPC for 13 months.
- Compliance: We need evidence for SOC2 controls around change management and access.

Preferences and constraints:
- Prefer US-only regions; primary us-east, secondary us-west for DR.
- We'd like autoscaling/burst policy that allows instant bursts to 2x baseline for up to 2 hours.
- Procurement wants an initial month-to-month pilot (Nov trial) followed by a 12-month committed pool if metrics meet expectations.

Can the Redwood team propose a concrete pool size, autoscale policy, and a short MAP (mutual action plan) we can review? Also attaching our internal SOW and current model mix for context.

Thanks,
Lisa Turner
VP Product, Polaris AI
[Attachment: Polaris_SOW_v3.pdf (pdf, 1.1MB)]

Team — looping you in to translate Polaris' asks into an implementation plan. From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Turner <lisa.turner@polaris-ai.com>
Date: 2027-02-17T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity kickstart — Polaris requirements and timeline

Folks — ran a quick sizing exercise against the model mix Lisa attached. High level recommendation for the pilot (month-to-month):
- Baseline pool: 6x A10G (40GB) GPUs with optimized kernel set + int8 quantization for production transformer models
- Burst policy: allow autoscale to +100% (2x baseline) for up to 2 hours; warm standbys in us-west with async cache replication
- If Polaris requires lower latency for heavy prompt engineering workloads, recommend hybrid split: 2x A100-80GB for latency-sensitive routes + 4x A10G for throughput routes (keeps cost reasonable while meeting p95).

Notes:
- With the above config and continuous batching varnish, expected p95 ~90–130ms depending on prompt length; we'll tune batching windows and kv-cache TTL to meet 120ms.
- Quantization trade-offs: int8 yields ~2.5x throughput improvement for cost-sensitive models; we'll validate quality on their eval set during pilot.
- Attach: preliminary GPU-sizing workbook and cost delta scenarios.

Action items for Polaris: confirm preferred mix (throughput-first vs latency-first), sign SOW addendum for the pilot, and provide endpoint test prompts for our eval run.

Attachments: gpu-specs.xlsx

Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: gpu-specs.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)]

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Turner <lisa.turner@polaris-ai.com>
Date: 2027-02-19T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity kickstart — Polaris requirements and timeline

Thanks Neha — operational checklist and timeline below. I'm proposing an initial provision window of 3 business days for the baseline pool, followed by a 5-day validation and tuning window. DR/us-west warm standbys will be provisioned concurrently but not cutover until acceptance testing.

Provisioning checklist (high level):
1) Provision 6x A10G in us-east (tagged to Polaris account) — day 0–2
2) Network & VPC peering + KMS key exchange — day 1–3
3) Deploy model container/weights (customer-provided or from our catalog) — day 2–4
4) Run load validation & quantization quality tests (Neha will own eval) — day 3–7
5) Enable autoscale policy: baseline=6 units, burst cap=12 units, burst window=2h — day 3
6) Configure KV/prefix caching with async replication to us-west — day 2–4
7) Acceptance & sign-off — day 7

Maintenance & standby notes:
- Weekly maintenance windows scheduled and communicated 72h in advance; enterprise SLA will allow patched rolling restarts with 99.9% monthly uptime objective.
- For burst handling >2h, automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant will be available to preserve availability.

I'll draft a short ops runbook and include required contact points and escalation path. Related runbook draft will be shared in the DRIVE link (see related_links).

Jonas Weber
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Lisa Turner <lisa.turner@polaris-ai.com>

- Polaris prefers the hybrid split (2x A100 for latency routes + 4x A10G for throughput) during the pilot so we can validate both patterns.
- Procurement can issue a PO for the pilot within this week; they asked for a one-page summary of deliverables and evidence items for SOC2 (change logs, access lists).
- Region confirmed: primary us-east (us-east-1), secondary us-west (us-west-2).

Can Marissa own the MAP and sign-off flow? Also we need a short doc that lists exactly which SOC2 artifacts Redwood will share during the pilot vs after commit.

Subject: Polaris MAP & next steps (pilot onboarding schedule)

Lisa — thanks and great to have alignment. Attached is a one-page MAP and deliverables summary for the pilot. High level next steps: 
1) Polaris to send PO by Mar 5 -> Redwood issues pilot SOW addendum (Mar 6)
2) Provision baseline pool (2x A100 + 4x A10G) in us-east & warm standby in us-west (Mar 8–10)
3) Validation & tuning window (Mar 11–15) — Neha to run evals and share results by Mar 16
4) SOC2 evidence package (pilot subset): change logs for provisioning, access list for provisioning engineers, and audit log export — delivered Mar 15
5) Acceptance & sign-off (Mar 16) -> if accepted Polaris moves to 12-month committed pool starting Apr 1

Marissa will own the MAP doc and the acceptance sign-off checklist. Rishi will provide the SOC2 evidence scope and delivery timeline. Jonas will own provisioning; Neha will own model tuning and quality gate.

I'll send the formal MAP PDF to procurement and Lisa after this thread. Thanks everyone — excited to get Polaris onboarded.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
